This module is a pre-completion checklist for concurrency bugs work: a short set of checks to run before calling a concurrency bugs task done.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Surface known limitations of a chosen concurrency bugs approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
2. When concurrency bugs guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
3. Re-check edge cases relevant to concurrency bugs (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
4. State assumptions about concurrency bugs explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
5. Keep concurrency bugs changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
6. Validate concurrency bugs outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
7. Document any non-obvious concurrency bugs decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
8. Measure before optimizing any concurrency bugs bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid introducing new concurrency bugs abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of concurrency bugs correctness.
- Do not skip documenting concurrency bugs assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Do not silently drop concurrency bugs edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these concurrency bugs guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
